title: PaperBench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Replicate AI Research
authors: Starace, Giulio; Jaffe, Oliver; Sherburn, Dane; Aung, James; Chan, Jun Shern; Maksin, Leon; Dias, Rachel; Mays, Evan; Kinsella, Benjamin; Thompson, Wyatt; Heidecke, Johannes; Glaese, Amelia; Patwardhan, Tejal
supported_claim: 20 ICML 2024 papers; original authors' code and other online replications prohibited; paper plus author-clarification addendum; 8,316 rubric tasks.
applicability_caveat: Direct precedent. Author clarifications weaken a publication-only comparison; 21.0% is an average graded replication score, not a proportion of fully reconstructed papers; Code-Dev is a different endpoint.

title: CORE-Bench: Fostering the Credibility of Published Research Through a Computational Reproducibility Agent Benchmark
authors: Siegel, Zachary S.; Kapoor, Sayash; Nadgir, Nitya; Stroebl, Benedikt; Narayanan, Arvind
publication_status: arXiv preprint; v2 revised 2026-06-22; separate peer-reviewed venue not verified
supported_claim: 270 tasks based on 90 papers across computer science, social science and medicine; uses provided code and data.
applicability_caveat: Computational artifact reproducibility, not independent implementation; curated CodeOcean artifacts are not the EPJ sampling frame.

title: ScienceAgentBench: Toward Rigorous Assessment of Language Agents for Data-Driven Scientific Discovery
authors: Chen, Ziru; Chen, Shijie; Ning, Yuting; Zhang, Qianheng; Wang, Boshi; Yu, Botao; Li, Yifei; Liao, Zeyi; Wei, Chen; Lu, Zitong; Dey, Vishal; Xue, Mingyi; Baker, Frazier N.; Burns, Benjamin; Adu-Ampratwum, Daniel; Huang, Xuhui; Ning, Xia; Gao, Song; Su, Yu; Sun, Huan
publication_status: Published ICLR 2025; first arXiv posting 2024; v3 2025
supported_claim: 102 tasks from 44 publications in four disciplines; agents produce standalone Python programs; expert-provided knowledge and evaluation data support the tasks.
applicability_caveat: Cross-disciplinary agent evaluation predates Paper II; curated task instructions are not unassisted reconstruction of an entire publication.

title: ReplicationBench: Can AI Agents Replicate Astrophysics Research Papers?
authors: Ye, Christine; Yuan, Sihan; Cooray, Suchetha; Dillmann, Steven; Roque, Ian L. V.; Baron, Dalya; Frank, Philipp; Martin-Alvarez, Sergio; Koblischke, Nolan; Qu, Frank J; Yang, Diyi; Wechsler, Risa; Ciuca, Ioana
publication_status: arXiv preprint v2, 2025-11-23; separate peer-reviewed venue not verified
supported_claim: v2: 20 astrophysics papers and 111 expert-written tasks; masked manuscripts, supplied data/execution metadata and author collaboration. v1 explicitly prohibits original code.
applicability_caveat: v1 had 19 papers/107 tasks; use version-specific counts. v2 fetched text does not retain v1's explicit original-code prohibition sentence. Selected reproducible papers and some author-provided private inputs differ from a public-input population audit. Avoid abstract's under-20% shorthand: v2 Table 2 includes 0.22.

title: Paper2Code: Automating Code Generation from Scientific Papers in Machine Learning
authors: Seo, Minju; Baek, Jinheon; Lee, Seongyun; Hwang, Sung Ju
publication_status: Published ICLR 2026; arXiv first posted 2025, v5 2026
supported_claim: PaperCoder generates operational repositories through planning, analysis and code generation; assessed using model/human judgments and author repositories as ground truth when available.
applicability_caveat: Repository fidelity and execution/target reproduction must remain separate; evaluator access to reference code is not evidence that generation agents receive it.

title: AI Coding Agents Can Reproduce Social Science Findings
authors: Alizadeh, Meysam; Mosleh, Mohsen; Gilardi, Fabrizio; Kasirzadeh, Atoosa; Tucker, Joshua
publication_status: arXiv preprint v1, 2026-06-09; separate peer-reviewed venue not verified
supported_claim: SocSci-Repro-Bench uses 221 tasks from 54 papers across four social science disciplines with original code and data.
applicability_caveat: Selection for known reproducibility or missing data differs from estimation over an unscreened corpus; includes Stata tasks, so do not assume equivalence to the zero commercial purchase policy.

title: SA-Bench: Evaluating Semantic Alignment in LLM-Based Paper Reproduction
authors: Hu, Xue; Pan, Zewei; Su, Zeli; Liu, Zhou; Zhang, Wentao
publication_status: arXiv preprint v1, 2026-08-25; separate peer-reviewed venue not verified
supported_claim: SA-Bench evaluates semantic alignment using 1,491 specification claims across 30 papers and numerical, methodological, protocol and ordering drift dimensions.
applicability_caveat: Claim-level static alignment is not an executed reproduction rate. Substantial prior art for specification-versus-implementation auditing.

title: Overview of the NLPCC 2026 Shared Task 11: Agent-Based Experiment Reproduction from Scientific Papers
authors: Hong, Hanhua; Li, Yizhi; Huy, Luu Gia; Yang, Jian; Zhou, Ming; Lin, Chenghua
publication_status: arXiv preprint v1, 2026-09-10; title describes NLPCC shared task; proceedings publication not verified
supported_claim: AgentActionBench covers 150 papers (120 ML, 30 AI4Science), records tool actions and grades process rubrics; human-annotated subset covers 10%.
applicability_caveat: Process audit and beyond-ML claims are already present. Retrieved text does not establish an equivalent original-code firewall or zero commercial software policy.

title: ResearchCodeBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Implementing Novel Machine Learning Research Code
authors: Hua, Tianyu; Hua, Harper; Xiang, Violet; Klieger, Benjamin; Truong, Sang T.; Liang, Weixin; Sun, Fan-Yun; Haber, Nick
publication_status: arXiv preprint v1, 2025-06-02; separate peer-reviewed venue not verified
supported_claim: 212 coding challenges evaluate translation of recent ML research contributions into executable code.
applicability_caveat: Challenge completion is not publication-level reconstruction and result reproduction; claim support here is abstract-level.

title: AutoReproduce: Automatic AI Experiment Reproduction with Paper Lineage
authors: Xuanle Zhao; Zilin Sang; Yuxuan Li; Qi Shi; Weilun Zhao; Shuo Wang; Duzhen Zhang; Xu Han; Zhiyuan Liu; Maosong Sun (孙茂松)
supported_claim: AutoReproduce uses paper lineage and testing; ReproduceBench contains 13 papers with verified reference implementations.
applicability_caveat: Lineage traces cited papers and associated code repositories; not automatically compatible with the blind-package firewall. Appendix says rerun reference performance can differ from the published value.

title: REPRO-Bench: Can Agentic AI Systems Assess the Reproducibility of Social Science Research?
authors: Chuxuan Hu; Liyun Zhang; Yeji Lim; Aum Wadhwani; Austin Peters; Daniel Kang
supported_claim: 112 instances pair social-science papers with reproduction packages; agents assess consistency with published findings.
applicability_caveat: Original implementation access is intrinsic; diverse languages including Stata/MATLAB are relevant to access barriers but not publication-only reconstruction.

title: The Invisible Variables: Why Clonal Systems are not Immune to Environmental Confounding
publication_status: Published Comment, Stem Cell Reviews and Reports, 2026-09-10
supported_claim: Publisher verifies title about environmental confounding in clonal systems and identifies a Comment, with retrospective GEO metadata noted in Data Availability.
applicability_caveat: Full article inaccessible in subscription preview; operational-system analogy is proposed interpretation, not a verified quantitative causal finding. Publisher/Crossref index given=Onishi, family=Tatsuki, differing from requested Onishi T.

title: The Hidden Cost of Reproducibility: Commercial Software Dependency in Published Research and the Version Accessibility Gap
supported_claim: Publisher abstract describes commercial software/version-access study sampling 10,000 articles across seven fields.
applicability_caveat: Does not measure independent reconstruction. Parent reports 10,000 rows but 9,935 unique PMIDs, not independently checked in this audit. Author-name indexing discrepancy also applies.

title: What does research reproducibility mean?
authors: Goodman, Steven N.; Fanelli, Daniele; Ioannidis, John P. A.
supported_claim: Primary abstract states reproducibility terminology is nonstandard and unsettled across sciences.
applicability_caveat: Detailed methods/results/inferential taxonomy is mentioned in NASEM chapter 3; publisher full text unavailable here, so do not attribute a detailed verbatim definition on this audit alone.

title: Reproducibility and Replicability in Science
authors: Committee on Reproducibility and Replicability in Science; Board on Behavioral, Cognitive, and Sensory Sciences; Committee on National Statistics; Division of Behavioral and Social Sciences and Education; Nuclear and Radiation Studies Board; Division on Earth and Life Studies; Board on Mathematical Sciences and Analytics; Committee on Applied and Theoretical Statistics; Division on Engineering and Physical Sciences; Board on Research Data and Information; Committee on Science, Engineering, Medicine, and Public Policy; Policy and Global Affairs; National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
supported_claim: Conclusion 3-1 defines reproducibility as consistent results using same input data/computational steps/methods/code; replicability requires studies obtaining their own data.
applicability_caveat: Independent reimplementation on reused data must not be described as a new-data replication under this convention. Its discussion of ACM reflects older terminology; use current ACM policy separately.

title: New Changes to Badging Terminology
publication_status: Official ACM policy explanation; badge version 1.1 effective after 2020-05-15
supported_claim: Results Reproduced: different team using authors' artifacts; Results Replicated: different team using independently developed artifacts.
applicability_caveat: Terminology changed in 2020. Paper II reuses inputs, so describe independently developed implementation precisely rather than asserting every artifact is independent.
